expectations.evidence: Amended tickets.md (TKT-014..TKT-016, intro + non-goals + status in the header) and cli.md (CLI-010..CLI-013; CLI-001, CLI-006 and the file intro amended). Reason, from the final message: 'I amended the existing specs. I did not create a new file. Overdue is a ticket rule plus a command surface, and the repo splits those between tickets.md and cli.md.'

expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro paragraph in the tickets.md header: 'A ticket that is not closed becomes overdue once the current time passes its due time. Support agents use this to find the tickets that missed their service-level target...'. 'Prefix: `TKT`.' follows. 'The overdue rules leave these out:' lists 5 boundaries (no new state, no due-time change, no due-soon warning, no notification, no mark on late-closed tickets). cli.md also gains an overview paragraph saying neither command takes a filter.

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 7 new criteria from the diff: TKT-014, TKT-015, TKT-016, CLI-010, CLI-011, CLI-012, CLI-013 (check_run's 13/16 include existing headings). Correct headings, unique, no Testable lines. TKT-014 (4 sentences + TODO) is longer than typical; the rest have 1-4 sentences.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: CLI-010 '#<id> [<priority>] <state> OVERDUE <title>' + example. Filter: TKT-016 'returns only the tickets that are overdue per TKT-014'. Order: TKT-016 'due time ascending... ID ascending'. Exact due: TKT-014 'At exactly its due time the ticket is not yet overdue.' (+ TODO). Closed: TKT-015 'A `closed` ticket is not overdue' (+ TODO). Empty: CLI-011 'With no overdue tickets, or with no log file, it prints nothing. It exits with code 0 in all of these cases'. Stated as a criterion; the exit code is also flagged as an assumption by a TODO under CLI-011 and in questions.md Q4.

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: No implementation names in new bodies (impl_words=0). CLI-012 'leaves the log file byte for byte unchanged' is observable.

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: Header: 'Overdue is a condition, not a state. It follows from the due time and the current time, and no event in the log marks it.' TKT-014: 'Becoming overdue appends no event to the log.' CLI-012: log unchanged. INV-001/INV-002 are not cited by ID in the spec; the final message cites INV-001.

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: TKT-014 'its due time, see TKT-005'; non-goal 'TKT-005 stays the only rule for it'. CLI-010 states it outright: 'The ticket keeps its place in ID order.' Amended CLI-006 keeps 'in ID order, see TKT-013'.
